subject: Proposed SLA language & credits — Redwood / Atlas Retail
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLA language & credits — Redwood / Atlas Retail

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the productive call this week. As promised, attaching our standard SLA template for hosted inference along with an outline of how monthly service credits are calculated. Key highlights (from the template):

- Standard uptime target: 99.9% monthly for Hosted API
- Monthly service credit: % of monthly fees tied to uptime bands (described in attached PDF)
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile targets included but not credit-backed for bursty workloads

Attachment: SLA_Template_Redwood_v1.pdf (PDF)

I know Atlas asked about a higher uptime target (99.95%) and a different credit structure. I wanted to get this in writing so we can surface any request formally to our engineering and legal for exception review. If you could share a short note on the business requirement driving 99.95% (and whether Atlas expects this only for peak hours or full-month), that would help.

Next steps: if you confirm the ask I'll loop in Grace (legal) and Marcus (eng) to evaluate feasibility and propose any compensating controls (dedicated capacity, scheduled maintenance windows, or a credit cap).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0124
[Attachment: SLA_Template_Redwood_v1.pdf]

From: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@atlasretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA language & credits — Redwood / Atlas Retail

Jordan —

Thanks for circling back. Atlas is planning a global checkout migration in Q4 and the availability bar for production traffic is elevated. Our procurement and engineering teams are aligned on the ask:

- Target availability: 99.95% (monthly) for production-facing inference endpoints
- Credits: we typically expect at least a 10% monthly fee credit for each 0.01% below the target in our existing agreements — open to discussing a tiered approach but want to avoid unlimited liability for downtimes
- Caps: procurement prefers a monthly cap at <= 50% of fees; legal will want to see precedent

I'll attach the terms our legal team drafted as an initial ask. If Redwood can meet 99.95% with a reasonable credit cap and express exceptions for force majeure/maintenance windows, Atlas will move the SOW forward.

Attachment: Atlas_Requested_Terms.docx

Best,
Alice Cheng
Head of Platform Engineering | Atlas Retail
alice.cheng@atlasretail.com
[Attachment: Atlas_Requested_Terms.docx]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Atlas requested SLA terms — need feasibility + exceptions input

Grace/Marcus —

Looping you both in on Atlas' request (attached). They are asking for 99.95% uptime with a credit structure that looks more aggressive than our standard template.

Questions:
- Legal: is a 99.95% commitment with a credit schedule and a 50% monthly cap something we can entertain as a one-off? Any redlines we should proactively flag?
- Eng: can Hosted API realistically hit 99.95% for production workloads without dedicated capacity? If not, what compensating controls could we offer (e.g., dedicated pool, prioritization, or upgrade path to Redwood Dedicated)?

I suggested we propose alternatives (99.9% + lower credits + option to add dedicated capacity) if 99.95% is a hard blocker for them. Please advise and I will draft a reply.

Thanks,
Jordan

--- Forwarded message attached above ---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas requested SLA terms — need feasibility + exceptions input

Jordan/Grace —

Quick technical read: 99.95% monthly uptime means ~21.6 minutes of allowable downtime per month. For our multi-tenant Hosted API, that target is challenging under realistic maintenance/upgrade windows and noisy neighbor events unless we provide additional isolation. Key points: 

- Root causes we see that drive short outages: autoscaling lag during sudden traffic spikes, regional infra maintenance, and upstream GPU preemption on some cloud instance types.
- We can reach 99.95% consistently if the customer is on: (a) dedicated capacity (reserved pool) or (b) a provisioned SLA tier with hot-standby routing across two regions. Both require an increase in cost or a reserved commitment.
- Latency: our credit structure today ties to availability bands, not 95th-p latency. If Atlas also expects latency guarantees during incidents, that increases operational risk.

Suggested mitigations to offer Atlas: 
1) Production commitment: Redwood can offer a one-off exception to get closer to 99.95% if Atlas moves to a dedicated pool (monthly reserved capacity) — engineering-ready.
2) Fallback: add automated cross-region fallback as part of the prod rollout (adds complexity but reduces single-region outages).
3) Credit cap: we recommend a monthly credit cap (max 50% of monthly fees) and carve-outs for scheduled maintenance and force majeure.

Happy to provide a cost delta estimate for dedicated capacity if we want to present a concrete option.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity_diagram.png]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@atlasretail.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA language & credits — Redwood / Atlas Retail

Alice/Jordan/Marcus —

Thanks — I've reviewed Atlas' requested wording and discussed internal precedent. A few notes and a counterproposal below: 

- Precedent: our standard hosted SLA is 99.9%. We have granted 99.95% in rare cases when the customer accepted dedicated capacity and an explicit credit cap.
- Liability: we should preserve standard carve-outs (maintenance windows, force majeure, customer-induced outages) and include a change-control clause for SLO definition changes.
- Credit schedule: instead of the per-0.01% step that Atlas proposed (which quickly multiplies), propose a tiered schedule: 99.5–99.9% = 10% credit; 99.0–99.5% = 25% credit; <99.0% = 50% credit (monthly cap at 50%). This keeps liability bounded while offering meaningful remediation.
- Exception path: approve exception to discuss 99.95% only if Atlas commits to either (i) reserved Redwood Dedicated pool for the production endpoints or (ii) a 12-month minimum committed spend that justifies the dedicated allocation.

If Atlas accepts either dedicated capacity or a 12-month commit, we can draft SLA language that includes 99.95% and maintains the proposed monthly credit cap. Please let me know which path they prefer and I will prepare redlines.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@atlasretail.com>, Legal - Atlas <legal@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA language & credits — Redwood / Atlas Retail

Alice / Atlas legal —

Appreciate the candid ask and the quick review from your side. Based on internal feedback (Marcus and Grace cc'd) here's a pragmatic path forward we can sign off on quickly: 

1) Option A (Recommended): Atlas moves production inference to a Redwood Dedicated reserved pool. In this configuration we will include a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment and adopt the following tiered credit schedule with a monthly cap of 50% of fees:
   - 99.5%–99.95% uptime: 10% credit
   - 99.0%–99.5% uptime: 25% credit
   - <99.0% uptime: 50% credit

2) Option B (Hosted): If Atlas opts to remain on Hosted API, we can accept 99.9% uptime with the same tiered credit schedule and a 50% monthly cap. We will not extend 99.95% on Hosted without a reserved commitment or a 12-month minimum spend.

3) Carve-outs: both options include standard carve-outs for scheduled maintenance (we will notify 72 hours in advance for non-emergency maintenance), force majeure, and customer-caused outages. Latency SLOs remain separate; credits are availability-based only.

Next steps: I've attached a DocuSign envelope with two SLA addendums (one for Option A and one for Option B). Please indicate which option you prefer and we will proceed with the SOW. If you'd like, Marcus can provide a cost delta and timeline for provisioning a dedicated pool.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/atlix/ATLAS-2104-SLA
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cSLAProposal

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
